parts.note: the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity story

indicators.note: almost means the word for relaxed stops short of its final letter

parts.note: relaxed means calm

explanation.surface: The wise men of the Nativity come across as charming and nearly laid-back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something charming is enchanting, as if worked by magic, a straightforward synonym.

definitions.meaning: to record songs, laying down tracks
to depart, as in the idiom for setting off

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes producing recordings and idiomatically means departing in a hurry.

clue.text: Anchor angler at sea holds quietly

indicators.note: holds means the shuffled letters enclose the other piece
at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A fisherman out on the water keeps his anchor still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges ANGLER into GRANEL, which 'holds' P.
explanation.definitionFit: A grapnel is a small anchor with several flukes, used for boats or grappling.

clue.text: Flying to palace inhabited by king and queen

indicators.note: inhabited by means the rearranged letters have the other piece living inside them
flying suggests letters scattered through the air, so they are rearranged

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Travelling by air to a royal residence where a monarch and his consort live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying' rearranges TO PALACE, and R sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, a famous queen.

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
I is the Roman numeral one
very means extremely

explanation.surface: A big, highly individual outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is a special uniform or colour scheme worn by servants or employees of a company.

definitions.meaning: to go without food, as at Lent or Ramadan

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both abstaining from food and moving quickly, two unrelated senses.

indicators.note: not means the named letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: to fire something is to set it alight
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A tree was set on fire, though not at its foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' suggests the trunk's foot but stands for the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: A fir is an evergreen coniferous tree.

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: soon means early, before long
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Strength showed in a primitive golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoon was an old name for a lofted wooden golf club, roughly a modern three-wood.

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: rejected means the name is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: Evan is a typically Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A jack and a king turn away a man from Wales, like a card game gone sour.
explanation.walkthrough: Evan is a stock Welsh first name; 'rejected' signals reading it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of cards the jack is also called the knave, an older name for the same card.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people find that Montana is a fine US state to explore.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermont is one of the fifty US states, in New England, so an example of a state.

clue.text: Managed health club with river outside, clear

indicators.note: outside means the river's name goes round the other pieces

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
ran means managed, as in ran a business
a spa is a health club or resort

explanation.surface: A wellness centre was run with a river around it, clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparent means see-through, and so plain or clear.

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a song is a short piece of music

explanation.surface: A lad's musical composition was left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Boy's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, a boy in relation to his parents.

clue.text: Burning desire to see extremely pretty country

indicators.note: extremely means only the extreme letters, first and last, of the word pretty are used

parts.note: Romania is a country in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: Someone longs to visit a very beautiful nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is an obsessive urge to set fires, so literally a desire for burning.

clue.text: Medical officer to come over for sport

parts.note: to cross is to come over, as a bridge or road

explanation.surface: An army doctor is visiting for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Motocross is the sport of racing motorcycles over rough cross-country tracks.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
late can mean former or past, as in the late president

explanation.surface: Describe what happened before.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or recount it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Painter in squat, mostly silent at first

indicators.note: mostly means the word for squat loses its final letter

parts.note: squat as an adjective means short and thick, stubby

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of silent

explanation.surface: An artist crouches down, keeping quiet to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squat' looks like a verb but is the adjective stubby.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs was an eighteenth-century English artist famous for his horse paintings.

parts.note: Bambi is the deer from the Disney animated film

explanation.surface: A Disney figure who is not a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is Italian for baby, used in English for a young child.

indicators.note: devouring means one piece swallows the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
all means everything

explanation.surface: A wan-looking pig eats up the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallow describes a sickly yellowish or pale complexion.

clue.text: Cleaner, by a stop, caught early coach

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British term for a cleaning lady
to ban something is to stop it
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady, waiting at a bus stop, caught an early coach to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc was an open motor bus with bench seats, an early form of the touring coach.

parts.note: a trailer advertises a film, so it is an ad
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: Alter the hitch on a trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to modify it for a new use, a synonym.

clue.text: Old lady eating duck, old bird

indicators.note: eating means one piece is taken inside another, as food goes in a mouth

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, ma
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: An elderly woman dines on duck, then on an ancient bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand, extinct for centuries.

clue.text: Disgraceful event boy recalled, on examination

indicators.note: in an across answer on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: a scan is a medical examination

indicators.note: recalled means the word is called back, read in reverse

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A shameful episode came to light when a boy was called back for a check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' signals reading the word for boy backwards, and 'on' places it after the examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is an event that causes public outrage and disgrace.

clue.text: Faculty head lacking area for study

indicators.note: lacking means the letter is missing from the word

parts.note: a dean heads a university faculty

explanation.surface: A college head is short of room to study.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a small private room for work or reading, a study.

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
nice means pleasant

explanation.definitionFit: A plan put on ice is suspended or held over, so it is awaiting decision.

indicators.note: turned means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: nuts is slang for heads

explanation.surface: People's heads swivel in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or daze them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Useless person with, initially, a reasonable chance?

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word with

parts.note: in British informal use, to be in with a shout is to have a reasonable chance

explanation.surface: Even a hopeless individual might be given a fair opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in with a shout' is British slang for having a decent chance of success.
explanation.definitionFit: A washout is informally a failure, a person or event that comes to nothing.
